messages.content: Help me add a 'click' event listener to a button element 'myButton' that triggers a function named 'handleButtonClick' and stops the event from propagating by setting options's stopProgation to true?

function.name: buttonAddClickHandler
function.description: This function attaches a click event listener to a specified button element with options to control event flow and behavior. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

element.description: The button element to which the event listener will be added. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

callback.description: The function to be called when the button is clicked. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

options.description: An options object to specify characteristics about the event listener, such as stopping propagation. Optional parameter. Default to be empty dictionary This is JavaScript dict type parameter in string representation.

The element is the button element to which the event listener will be added. The callback is the function to be called when the button is clicked. The options is an optional object specifying characteristics about the event listener, such as stopping propagation. The default is empty dictionary. The options is a JavaScript dict type parameter in string representation.

We need to call the tool with the appropriate arguments. The element is 'myButton', but we need to provide it as a string representation of a JavaScript object. So we might pass "document.getElementById('myButton')" or just "myButton" if it's a variable. But the instructions say: "This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation." So we can pass "myButton" or "document.getElementById('myButton')". The callback is "handleButtonClick". The options is an object with stopProgation set to true. But note: the property name is spelled incorrectly: "stopProgation" instead of "stopPropagation". The user wrote "stopProgation". We should preserve the user's spelling? The user says: "stops the event from propagating by setting options's stopProgation to true". So we should use "stopProgation" as the key. The value is true. So the options string representation is something like '{"stopProgation": true}'. That is a JSON string. The tool expects a string representation of a JavaScript dict. So we can pass that.

Thus we call the tool:

{
  "element": "myButton",
  "callback": "handleButtonClick",
